title: Part Two: Before Darby: British Restorationism, 1600s–1891

sections.brief: Restorationism defined (Crome) and dated before Darby/Scofield; Brightman (1609 print), Finch 1621 (arrest, recantation, suppression), Cromwell and Menasseh ben Israel 1655-56, Increase Mather 1669/1709, 18th-century continuity, Brothers 1795; London Society 1809/1815; conversion aim and Jewish reception; Lewis's 'Teaching of Esteem' and Sandmel's critique. Figures: time

Ashley/Shaftesbury and Palmerston (1830 marriage tie); Young vice-consul 1838-39; Quarterly Review Jan 1839; Palmerston to Ponsonby 11 Aug 1840 (FO 78/390 text: 'check' on Mehemet Ali, Jewish 'wealth'), cabinet not told, sultan declines; Anglo-Prussian bishopric 1841 (Act, endowment, Alexander, Newman, end 1886); LJS presidency 1848, PEF 1865; Blackstone 1891 handover; Hechler and Herzl 1896-98 (JTA 1931 vs Eulenburg route). Figures: compare; time

'A land without a people': Watson (before 1833), Keith 1843, 1844 review, Shaftesbury July 1853 (recipient disputed), 1875 PEF, Zangwill 1901 and his revision c.1904; three claims tested (Zionist coinage: no; widely used slogan: contested, Muir vs Shapira/Neumann/Khalidi; meant empty: contested readings). Figures: time; compare
